items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: And one guy put a chain around our wheel, and the other guy, Sam Morgan wheel.

ctx.x: Still could be. I think he could do it again if he had a chance. Might come by.

Oh, it just like Buddy Petit playing. If he would have been a high note fellow boy, he'd have been a killer dealer. But his tone was so rich man. He had a bigger tone than Louis. Boy, there was some days though, brother. I don't see nothing here now like it. Well, Paul, every Sunday, them must have had about thirty bands in the oil, thirty or thirty-five. Well, them band was one at the lake. They was out there on trucks and things, advertising for dancers and things, see. And if the two meet on the corner, there…
Well what about Sam Morgan and you, who won that battle? Who won that battle? One of those corners? Yeah, between you and Sam Morgan.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Well, every Sunday you'd meet a bunch, but it'd be the same bunch like Rene, Buddy Petit, Sam Marock, Chris Kelly

ctx.x: Who did you meet in the street, some of the different bands?

Well, every Sunday you'd meet a bunch, but it'd be the same bunch like Rene, Buddy Petit, Sam Marock, Chris Kelly, and what's his name? The Dine, downtown there, Cindy Desvinge, the old tuxedo, all them bands used to be out on the street, you know, advertising dances on Sundays. Maybe one of them would be playing at a funeral or something, somebody would die, and they'd all get on that together.
Did you ever have any battles of music in the places like, say, the Bows Club or any of those?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Chris Kelly, Kid Renee, Sam Morgan. And I said, well I was long there with them.

ctx.x: You know, and who the hot ones were and who the straight ones were.
Well, the hot ones were, up and down the street. Chris Kelly, Kid Renee, Sam Morgan. And I said, well I was long there with them. And, uh, the little Carl Sidney Dutton, he was one of that bunch too.
He was a righty trumpet player.
